sections.h2: What is Nicholas County, and where does a house sit within it?
sections.html:
Nicholas County is in central West Virginia on the Allegheny Plateau, with Summersville as the county seat and Richwood as the other city. The Virginia legislature created it on January 30, 1818, from parts of Greenbrier, Kanawha and Randolph counties and named it for Governor Wilson Cary Nicholas. It covers 654 square miles, 647 of them land.

Braxton, Webster, Greenbrier, Fayette, Clay and Kanawha counties border it. Part of the Gauley River National Recreation Area and part of the Monongahela National Forest fall inside its lines. The seven magisterial districts are Beaver, Grant, Hamilton, Jefferson, Kentucky, Summersville and Wilderness, and the census-designated places include Belva, Craigsville, Fenwick, Nettie and Tioga.

sections.h2: How did timber, coal and the highway shape Nicholas County?
sections.html:
Nicholas County has changed industries several times, and each left buildings behind. The Weston and Gauley Bridge Turnpike, finished in 1859, ran north and south through Summersville. Around 1900 the railroad arrived, lumbering took off, and the Cherry River Boom and Lumber Company built one of the world's largest sawmills at Richwood.

Other plants followed, including a paper mill, a tannery, handle and hub factories and what was then the world's largest clothespin factory. Coal drove another surge later in the century and softened in the 1970s and early 1980s. The county's peak count of 28,126 people came in 1980.

The four-lane Appalachian Corridor L, which is U.S. 19, was finished through the county in the 1990s and brought heavy north and south traffic to roadside businesses. Nicholas County also belongs to the 4C Economic Development Authority with Fayette, Raleigh and Summers counties.

sections.h2: What do people in Nicholas County do for work?
sections.html:
Residents work in manufacturing, commerce, services and government, with some in mining and a few hundred on farms. The encyclopedia lists bituminous coal, limestone quarries, timber, fruit farms, tobacco and livestock among the county's resources.

Tourism has grown around Summersville Lake, which President Lyndon Johnson dedicated on September 3, 1966. It is the largest impoundment in the state, with about 2,800 acres of surface and 60 miles of shoreline, and it joined the state park system in 2023. Each fall the reservoir is lowered, which turns the lower Gauley into whitewater and brings a rafting season.

  • Carnifex Ferry Battlefield State Park marks an 1861 Civil War engagement.
  • Richwood hosts a ramp festival and Summersville a potato festival.
  • Vacation rentals, campgrounds and boat rentals serve lake and river visitors.
  • The county school system runs 15 schools with nearly 3,500 students, and public school enrollment was 3,382 in 2024-25.

The 2025 population estimate of 23,848 is 3.1 percent below the 2020 count. Median household income in the encyclopedia's fact box is $42,946, against $50,884 for the state.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Nicholas County?
sections.html:
Nicholas County splits the job between the Sheriff's Tax Office, which collects, and the Assessor, which values the property. Both are elected offices.

The assessor's page lists four dates to remember: the homestead exemption request is due December 1, the assessment year begins July 1, the farm report is due September 1, and taxes are shown with an April 1 payment deadline. Ms. Griffin's four-year term runs out in 2028. See the county assessor page for the current text.

sections.h2: What are the Nicholas County property tax deadlines and penalties?
sections.html:
The statewide calendar applies. Tickets come out on or after July 15, the first half is due September 1, and the second half is due March 1.

  • Pay before September 1 or before March 1 to take the 2.5 percent discount.
  • First-half tax that is still unpaid becomes delinquent on October 1.
  • Second-half tax becomes delinquent on April 1.
  • Interest on delinquent tax runs at 9 percent per year.

Parcels still delinquent on September 1 go on a second list that the sheriff prepares by September 10, and unredeemed liens are certified to the State Auditor on October 31 under West Virginia Code 11A-3-2. The owner can redeem before that date by paying the tax, interest and charges, which include $25 for the list and $10 for each mailed notice.

sections.h2: How much of the Nicholas County tax bill goes to schools?
sections.html:
About two thirds of the 2024 levy went to schools. The State Tax Division's tax year 2024 publication shows $17,865,512 levied across all purposes.

The real estate portion was $10,024,686. Class II, which the state defines as property owned, used and occupied by the owner for residential purposes, accounted for $4,777,644 of that, or about 48 percent. Class III outside municipalities was $3,104,634 and Class IV inside municipalities was $2,142,409. The state says the Class II rate is twice Class I and Classes III and IV are four times Class I, so an empty or rented house in Summersville or Richwood pays at a higher rate than the same house lived in by its owner.

sections.h2: How do you contest a Nicholas County assessment?
sections.html:
You raise it with the assessor and then with the county commission acting as the board of equalization and review.

West Virginia Code 11-3-24 requires the commission to meet as the board no later than February 1. It may adjourn after February 15 and must finish by the end of February. The board corrects errors and brings anything assessed at more or less than 60 percent of market value to 60 percent, and no increase can come without five days of written notice. Skipping the meeting waives the correction for that year except through an appeal to the Office of Tax Appeals. Questions about class or taxability are outside the board's reach and follow a protest route to the assessor.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the Nicholas County homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Owners aged 65 or older, and owners certified as permanently and totally disabled, can exempt the first $20,000 of assessed value of an owner-occupied home. West Virginia Code 11-6B-3 also requires two consecutive calendar years of state residency, with exceptions for returning residents and military retirees.

The exemption belongs to the owner on the July 1 assessment date. When the house changes hands by deed or will, it comes off on the next July 1 unless the new owner qualifies. Under that wording, a house sold in March keeps the old owner's exemption until the following July.

sections.h2: What should you know about selling a Nicholas County house with tax due?
sections.html:
The buyer's title company will look for unpaid tickets, so deal with them first. Start with the Sheriff's Tax Office and ask for the balance on each tax year, including fire fee charges, which the office's online system lists.

The deed has to be recorded with the county clerk, and the transfer tax is set by West Virginia Code 11-22-2: $1.10 per $500 of value, kept by the county since July 1, 2025, plus an additional county tax of 55 cents per $500 unless the commission raised it, plus a $20 fee. On a $90,000 sale at those base rates that is $198, $99 and $20, so $317. The seller pays unless the buyer accepts the deed with the tax unpaid.

Sellers here may hold a house in Summersville or Richwood, a rural parcel or an inherited home. Flooding is part of the local record: the encyclopedia says a deadly 2016 flood along the Cherry River devastated Richwood and other places in the county, so ask any buyer or insurer about flood history for a Richwood address.

faqs.q: When are Nicholas County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1, with a 2.5 percent discount for paying before either date. Unpaid halves become delinquent on October 1 and April 1.

faqs.q: Where is the Nicholas County Sheriff's Tax Office?
faqs.a: It is at 700 Main Street in Summersville, WV 26651, and the phone number is 304-872-7842. The sheriff's system offers online tax search, online payment and fire fee inquiry.

faqs.q: What is the homestead exemption deadline in Nicholas County?
faqs.a: The county assessor's page lists December 1 as the deadline for a homestead exemption request. The exemption is $20,000 of assessed value for owners 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled.

faqs.q: Do I owe property tax if I sell my Nicholas County house mid-year?
faqs.a: The tax for the year is a lien on the property, so any unpaid ticket must be settled at or before closing. Ask the sheriff's office for the balance and have the title company confirm it.

faqs.q: How is a Nicholas County home assessed?
faqs.a: The assessor values it at 60 percent of market value, and the owner's class sets the rate. Owner-occupied residential property is Class II, which the state publication says is taxed at twice the Class I rate, while other real estate outside or inside municipalities is taxed at four times Class I.
